mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates active monetary tightening, which raises discount rates and increases equity risk premiums, producing negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of months where FEDFUNDS increases month-over-month, or the Rank IC for the FEDFUNDS change signal is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 4.0% in a monthly reading, it signals accelerating economic weakness that triggers risk-off sentiment and negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.0%, or the Rank IC for the UNRATE threshold signal is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals broad-based consumer demand contraction, reducing corporate revenue expectations and producing negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of months where both HOUST and RSAFS decline month-over-month, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and rising), a month-over-month increase in core CPI (CPIAUCSL) signals persistent inflation requiring further rate hikes, compressing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL increases month-over-month during a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and rising), or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates robust labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months where PAYEMS increases month-over-month, or the Rank IC for the PAYEMS change signal is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline below 1400.0 thousand units in a monthly reading, it signals a housing market contraction that reduces consumer confidence and corporate investment, producing negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where HOUST falls below 1400.0, or the Rank IC for the HOUST threshold signal is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and quarterly GDP growth below 1.0% (GDPC1) signals a broad economic contraction that reduces corporate earnings expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where both INDPRO declines and GDPC1 growth is below 1.0%, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion (GDP growth > 2.5% and UNRATE < 4.0%), a month-over-month decline in retail sales (RSAFS) signals weakening consumer demand that triggers profit-taking and negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where RSAFS declines month-over-month during a late-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
